transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-02 10:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Aisha (CTO, LakeMont), Ben (Head of ML), Samantha (PM), Ravi (Security)

Summary:
Jordan walks through Redwood's Model Catalog in the Console, focusing on selecting open models, reading benchmark summaries, and explaining compatibility matrices (hardware, quantization, dedicated vs hosted vs private). Priya answers technical questions about batching, KV cache, quantization tradeoffs and running benchmarks. Security questions around SOC2, KMS, SAML/SSO, and VPC/private deploys are raised. Agreed next steps: send pricing, run compatibility/benchmark tests, provide sample prompts, schedule POC kickoff.

Topics:
- Model catalog overview (open models, verified profiles)
- Benchmarks & cost/latency tradeoffs
- Compatibility matrix: CPU/GPU types, quantization, Dedicated/Private availability
- Security & compliance (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS)
- POC & benchmarks logistics

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Lee with Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. With me is Priya Raman our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Aisha: Good, thanks. We were hoping to get a quick tour of the model catalog and then dive into benchmarks around latency and cost.
[00:12] Jordan: Yep that's the plan, we'll show the Console model catalog, how to pick open models, and look at the compatibility matrix. Priya will cover the benchmark methodology.
[00:20] Priya: Hi hi, quick note — we keep the model profiles in the catalog with pre-run perf metrics (median p95 latencies), and suggested quantization levels like FP16, Q4 and Q8 where we support them.
[00:30] Ben: Right, and for our use case we need sub-300ms median for 512 token responses, cost under X per 1k tokens ideally — want to see the tradeoffs.
[00:40] Jordan: Totally — we'll show a couple of model selections: smaller transformer families like Mistral 7B for cost-sensitive routes, Falcon 40B and Llama 2 70B for higher quality/latency tradeoffs. Also how the Console marks "Redwood-verified" performance.
[00:52] Samantha: When you say Verified, what exactly is in that profile? Is it the HW used, sequence lengths, batching config?
[00:58] Priya: Good question. The profile includes test hardware (e.g., A100-80GB, H100, T4), sequence length distribution used, batching config and KV cache assumptions, and the quantization/precision used. There's a link to the benchmark spreadsheet too. Sometimes the auto transcriber says kv chache — it's kv cache.
[01:12] Ravi: From security side we care about private deployments and K M S key management, audit logs, and SSO. Do you support SAML and tenant-level RBAC?
[01:20] Jordan: Yes, for Private we support VPC peering and customer KMS integration (HSM options on request). We also have tenant RBAC and SAML/SSO — we'll share the security pack.
[01:30] Ben: Walk us through picking a model in the catalog — specifically how to know which model will be compatible with our Dedicated pool vs hosted.
[01:36] Priya: Sure — in the Console you can filter by model family and see compatibility columns. For each model we list supported deployment modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private on-prem. There's also a compatibility matrix that shows recommended kernel/quantization and whether it's validated on A100/H100 or Ampere vs Nvidia.
[01:50] Jordan: I'll share my screen — ok open the model catalog — you'll see Mistral 7B entry, the profile shows median throughput, cost per 1k tokens on hosted, and an availability column.
[02:05] Priya: For Mistral 7B we usually recommend Q4 for A100 to hit the cost targets without huge quality regressions. For Llama 2 70B we have FP16 and some Q8 variants but Q8 may change output slightly; we note expected delta in the profile.
[02:23] Aisha: How accurate are those delta numbers? Like how much does response quality drop when moving to Q4?
[02:28] Priya: We run evals on curated prompt sets and expose quality regression percentages per model/quantization in the catalog. It's not perfect for your prompts — that's why the POC to run your prompt set matters.
[02:40] Ben: Could we run a parallel benchmark — same prompt set across Mistral 7B Q4, Falcon 40B FP16, Llama 70B FP16 on your infra?
[02:47] Priya: Absolutely, we can spin up a temporary benchmark cluster in Dedicated mode or run hosted requests against instrumented routes. We'll produce a compatibility matrix output that lists latencies (median/p95), cost estimate, and notes about MAU or concurrency limits.
[03:05] Jordan: Note — when we talk about cost we include tokenization, prompt + completion tokens, and sometimes streaming overhead. The Console shows a cost per 1k tokens estimate based on our measured throughput.
[03:20] Samantha: For the POC, timeline-wise we'd like something within two weeks. We want to prove latency and good enough quality for our triage workflow.
[03:28] Jordan: That should be fine. Priya, on timeline — we can run initial compatibility runs in about 3 business days once we get sample prompts and access.
[03:35] Priya: Yep, if Ben can upload a ~200 prompt set and specify seq len targets we'll run bench and put results into the sheet.
[03:42] Ben: I'll prepare that. A question on batching: what's Redwood's default batching strategy? Is it dynamic?
[03:47] Priya: We use continuous batching on the runtime — it's workload aware. There's a batching policy you can configure per route; for low-latency we recommend smaller max batch sizes and aggressive KV cache. For high-throughput background jobs you allow larger batch sizes.
[04:03] Ben: And the KV cache is shared per session? Do you purge on timeout?
[04:07] Priya: It's managed per request context — TTLs are configurable, and we can persist KV cache for interactive flows on Dedicated.
[04:15] Ravi: Any audit logs for inference inputs? Our compliance team requires retainable audit logs for 90 days.
[04:20] Jordan: We provide structured request logging with redaction options and retention controls for Private and Dedicated. Hosted has configurable retention tiers. We'll include that in the security pack.
[04:33] Aisha: Pricing — high level ballpark for Dedicated and hosted? We need rough numbers to budget.
[04:38] Jordan: I'll send the pricing sheet after this call. Quick high-level: hosted is usage-based per token + embedding units, Dedicated is committed monthly with a capacity model — lower per-token but requires commit. We'll share exact numbers.
[04:52] Samantha: In the compatibility matrix, do you also note which libraries/runtime features are needed, like Triton kernels or custom attention kernels?
[04:58] Priya: Yes — we annotate the kernels and if we used custom fused attention kernels, flash attention etc. Also note when we used compilation flags for perf.
[05:10] Ben: One nit — sometimes model names in perf sheets are slightly different (like Llama 2 vs Llama2). Can you keep canonical model ids?
[05:16] Jordan: Good call, we'll standardize names in the sheet.
[05:20] Ravi: For Private on-prem, do you ship a control plane or is it customer-hosted entirely?
[05:25] Jordan: Control plane is optional; we offer a managed control plane with VPC connectivity or a self-hosted control plane for air-gapped installs. KMS integration via customer keys is supported.
[05:34] Aisha: Ok that addresses most of our security concerns. On the model quality side, could you demo one of the side-by-side outputs?
[05:40] Priya: Sure — I'll run a quick demo with a sample prompt: [Priya types] — here's Mistral 7B Q4 answer, Falcon 40B FP16 answer, Llama 70B FP16. You can see the 7B is terse but fast; 70B gives more nuanced detail but higher latency.
[06:00] Ben: Those are helpful. Any gotchas when moving from hosted to Dedicated re: tokenization differences or pre/post processing?
[06:06] Priya: Tokenization is consistent across deployment modes — same tokenizer and token counts. Differences can occur if you enable model-specific compilation flags, but we document those in the compatibility matrix.
[06:18] Samantha: About the benchmark artifacts — will you share the raw logs and the summarized sheet?
[06:23] Priya: Yes we'll share both. The sheet will include median/p95 latencies, cost estimates, concurrency tested, and the runtime config used. Raw logs can be shared behind an S3 link.
[06:35] Ben: For concurrency testing, can you simulate our expected traffic pattern? We have spiky loads with bursts up to 250 RPS for short periods.
[06:43] Priya: We can model bursts and show how autoscaling behaves with Dedicated pools; for hosted we show typical shedding/fallback policies and can configure routing to cheaper variants when capacity is stressed.
[06:55] Ravi: One more security question — do you have SOC 2 type II?
[06:58] Jordan: Yes, we do. We'll attach the SOC 2 pack and point to our compliance page.
[07:05] Aisha: Great. To recap — Jordan will send pricing and security docs; Priya will run the compatibility + bench using our prompts; Ben will upload prompts; Ravi will send security requirements. Schedule POC kickoff for week of 6/8.
[07:20] Jordan: Yup exactly. Anything else?
[07:24] Samantha: No, thanks. Look forward to the bench.
[07:28] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the deck and next steps.

End of transcript.
